videos.title: This Popular Drink Could Be Clogging Your Arteries | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
This Popular Drink Could Be Clogging Your Arteries | Dr. Mandell This popular drink may seem harmless—or even healthy—but when it’s loaded with added sugar, drinking it day after day can contribute to metabolic changes that affect your heart and arteries. In this video, I explain what can happen inside your body when you regularly consume sugar-sweetened tea and other sugary beverages, including how excess sugar can affect insulin, triglycerides, inflammation, body fat, cholesterol, and the delicate lining of your blood vessels. We’ll discuss why liquid sugar can be so easy to overconsume, why a drink labeled “tea,” “natural,” or even “organic” isn’t automatically healthy, and why reading the added-sugars line on the nutrition label is so important. You’ll also learn how years of repeated metabolic stress can contribute to the conditions that promote plaque formation within the arteries, even when you feel perfectly healthy and have no obvious symptoms. Most importantly, I’ll show you simple ways to continue enjoying tea without loading your body with unnecessary sugar, including gradually reducing sweetness, mixing sweetened and unsweetened tea, and using natural flavors such as lemon, lime, mint, or cinnamon. Heart disease doesn’t develop because of one drink or one meal—it develops from patterns repeated over time. Becoming aware of what you drink every day may be one of the simplest changes you can make to support healthier arteries, better metabolism, and a stronger cardiovascular system for years to come.

The best way to improve VO2 max is through regular aerobic exercise, especially vigorous exercise. But if you're unable to train hard, or you simply want to strengthen your breathing muscles, inspiratory muscle training can be a useful supplement.

Here's how it works:
👋 It starts you off with a core team: Fizz (the builder), Honey (the writer), and Bumble (the researcher).

🔒 Because it's built on the open-source Nostr protocol, it's model-agnostic, decentralized, and entirely under your control.

This kind of alternative is great for developers, startups, and anyone looking to run a self-sovereign AI workforce under their own control.

Would this replace Slack for you?

One of the earliest warning signs of heart problems can be erectile dysfunction. It often appears 3 to 5 years before heart disease because the blood vessels that supply an erection are narrower, so problems tend to show up there first.

If you have erectile dysfunction or other warning signs of heart disease, the following tests can help assess your heart health:

• CAC (coronary artery calcium) test
• Ultrasound of the carotid arteries
• Fasting insulin test

If you still get erections during the night or early morning, you may not have a vascular problem. 

Testosterone drives libido, not the erection itself. Nitric oxide plays an important role in healthy erectile function, but nitric oxide levels naturally decline with age. Poorly controlled blood sugar, smoking, vaping, sleep apnea, chronic inflammation, certain medications, and a sedentary lifestyle can also decrease nitric oxide.

If you have erectile dysfunction or any other warning signs of heart disease, it’s important to discuss them with your doctor.

videos.title: Could This Become a Somatic Retreat in Kyoto, Japan?
videos.summary_source_text:
Could This Become a Somatic Retreat in Kyoto, Japan? Could this quiet log house in the Kyoto countryside someday become a small somatic retreat space?

My family and I are staying at Yuka’s parents’ log house in Keihoku, surrounded by forests, mountains, a flowing river, and a much slower pace of life than central Kyoto.

While we were here, Yuka raised an unexpected possibility: perhaps this could become a place for a small English-language somatic retreat someday.

Not a luxury resort. Not a large event or a packed schedule.

I imagine something quieter and more personal—a small group gathering to explore gentle somatic movement, walk, rest, reflect, and reconnect with the body away from the usual noise and pressure.

For me, the idea also feels meaningful because I was born and raised in Japan, but I have taught mainly in English for many years. Bringing English-speaking students here could create a bridge between my background, my family, my work, and the people who have learned with me from around the world.

This is not an official retreat announcement yet. We are simply exploring whether there is genuine interest.

If the idea speaks to you, leave the words “Kyoto retreat” in the comments. You can also share what you would hope to experience in a small somatic retreat like this.

If you are tired of treating your body like a problem to solve, you can learn more about my guided course, Moving Freely in Your Body, here:
https://taroiwamoto.com/thecourse

This course is for thoughtful, self-aware adults who are ready to move beyond chasing relief, correcting their body, or piecing together random exercises — and begin learning a different relationship with their body through guided somatic movement.

If you’re newer to this work, start with my free somatic masterclass:
Move More Freely in Your Body
https://taro-iwamoto.thinkific.com/courses/masterclass

Read my book:
Your Body Is Not Broken: A Gentle Somatic Path to Moving with More Ease, Trust, and Freedom

A short Kindle book for anyone tired of trying to fix their body and wanting a gentler way to begin again.
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GX363HMX

About Taro Iwamoto

I help self-aware adults who feel stuck in recurring pain, tension, bracing, or fear of movement — even after trying many approaches — discover a gentler somatic, nervous-system-based path toward more ease, trust, and freedom in their body.

My work is not about forcing the body to change, finding the perfect exercise, or diagnosing what is wrong.

It is about helping your body and nervous system experience support, safety, connection, and new possibilities through gentle somatic movement.

More than 50% of adults in the United States have high blood pressure, and many don’t know it. High blood pressure is often called the “silent killer” because it can go undetected.

Research has shown that the wall sit is one of the best exercises to help reduce systolic blood pressure. A wall sit is an isometric exercise, meaning your muscles contract without movement.

The wall sit exercise can lower systolic blood pressure by about 8 points, outperforming many other forms of exercise. If you have high diastolic blood pressure, cardio exercise may be more beneficial.

Reducing high blood pressure may also lower your risk of:
• Cardiovascular events
• Coronary heart disease
• Stroke
• Heart failure
• All-cause mortality

To help support healthy blood pressure levels, perform 4 wall sits in a row, holding each for 2 minutes with a 2-minute rest between each set. Repeat this routine 3 times per week.

Mat’s got his hands on the all-new Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric, and he’s about to see if the most powerful Porsche ever is truly deserving of so much power. 

For starters, let’s check out the design… 

From the front, it’s fair to say that the exterior design is an improvement over the old petrol-powered Cayenne! It has a real presence from the front, with aggressive air scoops on either side, while the Turbo edition has additional vents and air intakes across the bumper. Along the side, there are wider surrounds on the wheel arches, and the Turbo edition we’re reviewing has a grey satin effect on the roof bars and window surrounds. There are also blackened side skirts, which, in this case, have "Turbo" written on them. Along the back there’s an aggressive diffuser, and the Porsche badge is embossed into the full-length light bar. 

On the inside, this new Cayenne has moved away from traditional Porsche interior designs of old, with the incorporation of more screens. There are dual screens in the centre console, a passenger screen, and a large, curved digital dial display. The dial display comes with lots of customisable options, and a lot of the functionality for the car is managed through the infotainment screen. Thankfully, though, there are physical buttons for the climate control. The seats are firm and figure-hugging, and there are soft-touch materials throughout most of the cabin - although you don’t have to search too hard to find some scratchy plastics! 

The Cayenne Turbo Electric is powered by two electric motors, and these combine to produce an incredible 1,156hp and 1,500Nm! It may be heavy, tipping the scales at 2,645kg, but it still launches like a rocket ship! It’s equipped with a 113kWh battery pack, and it has a claimed range of 350 - 387 miles. 

The Cayenne Electric range starts from £83,265 (as of August 2026), rising all the way up to £130,965 for the Turbo. But of course, it doesn’t stop there - the car we’re reviewing, with options, costs over £172,000! So is it worth it? And would you choose an electric Cayenne over an older, petrol-powered alternative? Let us know in the comments!

If you want to get 6 pack abs, there are a few things you need to get right. In this video, I’m breaking down 13 of my best tips for getting six pack abs by combining smarter nutrition, better ab workouts, and more effective exercise technique. You cannot build a visible, ripped six pack by focusing on ab exercises alone. You need to train the muscles correctly while also lowering body fat through a sustainable nutrition plan.

The first tip starts where your day begins. After going several hours without water while you sleep, you may wake up mildly dehydrated. Drinking 16 to 20 ounces of water shortly after waking can help you rehydrate before training, eating, or starting the rest of your day. Proper hydration supports exercise performance, energy, and the quality of your ab workouts. Whether your goal is to lose belly fat or perform better in the gym, staying hydrated matters.

Next, pay attention to the order of your ab exercises. Start with lower ab exercises that require you to move the legs or pelvis. These movements are often more demanding and require greater control. Save top-down movements, such as crunch variations, for later in the workout. This lets you perform the hardest exercises while your abs are fresh and your form is still strong.

When it comes to nutrition for six pack abs, use a simple plate strategy to control portions without counting every calorie. Imagine your plate as a clock. Fill the largest portion with fibrous carbohydrates such as vegetables. Fill the next largest portion with a quality source of protein. Use the smallest section for starchy carbohydrates, then include a modest amount of dietary fat. This makes it easier to build balanced meals and stay consistent with your fat loss goals.

For a complete list of better carbohydrate choices, visit https://athleanx.com/carbs.

During your ab workouts, stop focusing only on how many reps you complete. Make every repetition count. A fast, careless rep that creates little tension in the abs should not count the same as a controlled contraction. Slow the movement down and focus on feeling the abdominal muscles do the work. Quality contractions will do more for building defined abs than racing through sloppy repetitions.

On lower ab exercises, think about lifting the pelvis rather than simply lifting the legs. Moving the legs without curling the pelvis can allow the hip flexors to take over. When possible, squeeze the knees together to engage the adductors. This can improve pelvic stability and create a stronger contraction in the lower abs.

For upper ab exercises, imagine a line running across the bottom of your ribcage. Try to fold your torso over that line. Focus on lifting the shoulder blades off the floor by contracting the abs instead of pulling on your head or neck. This can make top-down ab exercises safer and more effective.

Your diet can also include a few simple additions that may support fat loss when used consistently. Green tea, cinnamon, and red pepper flakes are easy additions. I personally use Ceylon cinnamon in oatmeal and red pepper flakes in different foods throughout the day. None of these will give you abs by themselves, but small habits can support a stronger nutrition plan when combined with training, calorie control, and consistency.

Breathing is another important part of ab training. If you push your abdomen outward every time you exhale, you may reinforce a distended appearance through the midsection. Instead, tighten the waist by engaging the transverse abdominis as you breathe out. Think about drawing the abdomen inward while maintaining control of the movement. With practice, this can become automatic and improve your control of the core.

The rest of the 13 tips for getting 6 pack abs are covered in the video. Watch the full breakdown and let me know which tip helped you most.

Getting abs is not about finding one magical exercise or following an extreme diet. It comes from combining effective ab workouts, better technique, proper hydration, smart food choices, portion control, and a plan you can follow long enough to see results. The goal is not simply to lose weight. It is to reduce body fat while building strong, visible abdominal muscles.

Faucet handles, restroom doors, damp towels, cell phones, shopping carts, gas pumps, menus, and self-checkout screens are touched repeatedly throughout the day. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains how clean hands can become recontaminated, why touching your eyes, nose, or mouth matters, and the simple public-restroom habit that can reduce unnecessary exposure. Proper handwashing means using soap, scrubbing every surface for at least 20 seconds, cleaning around the thumbs, fingertips, fingernails, and between the fingers, then drying completely. This is not about fearing every germ—it is about protecting your hands after they are clean, especially before eating, during cold and flu season, while traveling, and whenever someone around you is sick. Share this important reminder with your family and friends.

videos.summary_source_text:
Nyss fyllt 18: vad borde jag veta om pengar? (2026) En artonåring messade mig med en enkel fråga: "Vad borde jag veta om pengar och långsiktigt sparande?" I den här videon svarar jag och Oliver med fem konkreta råd.

Det viktigaste är att börja spara så tidigt som möjligt, ränta-på-ränta-effekten är svår att greppa men gör en enorm skillnad över tid. Vi går igenom den så kallade tolv-tolv-tolv-principen: sparar du en summa i tolv år kan du sedan ta ut samma summa varje månad resten av livet.

Vi pratar också om varför en dyr bil som artonåring ofta är ett av de sämsta ekonomiska besluten man kan ta, varför det lönar sig att öka inkomsten tidigt, och varför breda, billiga globala indexfonder (eller en fondrobot som Lysa eller Opti) slår att försöka pricka rätt aktier själv.

Oliver har suttit i styrelsen för Unga Aktiesparare i fem år och berättar varför gemenskapen där är värdefull för unga som vill ta tag i sin ekonomi tidigt.

Fler guider på rikatillsammans.se.

⚠️ Viktig info:

Detta innehåll är inte individuell investeringsrådgivning. Ett sparande i linje med forskningens rekommendationer har historiskt sett varit framgångsrikt. Det finns mycket som talar för att så även kommer vara framgent, men det finns inga garantier. Historisk avkastning är ingen garanti för framtida avkastning. Alla investeringar innebär risk och kan både öka och minska i värde. Investera inte pengar du inte har råd att förlora. Mer info på rikatillsammans.se.

Författat av Jan Bolmeson per publicerat datum. Vi äger andelar i nämnda fonder genom regelbundet månadssparande. Vi är fristående från nämnda bolag och värdepapper; ingen ersättning har utgått om ej annat anges ovan. Tidigare omnämningar finns som etikett på rikatillsammans.se. Vi avser inte följa upp detta innehåll.

videos.title: After Injury: How Soon to Exercise Again?
videos.summary_source_text:
After Injury: How Soon to Exercise Again? The answer is: not today, but also not too long.

For most minor injuries, you want to get back to movement once the initial inflammation settles and you have a better idea of what you're dealing with.

As a general rule, if discomfort is around 4/10 or less, careful movement is often appropriate:

Walking
Gentle strengthening
Controlled stretching

Movement during recovery can help restore function and provide the mechanical loading that supports collagen remodeling and better tissue organization as you heal. 💪

The goal isn't to push through pain. It's to get moving again without waiting until you feel 100%. The answer is: not today, but also not too long.

videos.title: This is the best car America has ever made!
videos.summary_source_text:
This is the best car America has ever made! Hennessey has released an all-new Koenigsegg competitor - the Blackbird!

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-0308

The Blackbird follows on from Hennessey’s first two hypercars, the Venom GT & Venom F5, and it’s been inspired by the legendary SR-71 Blackbird aircraft. 

The question is, what makes it a true Koenigsegg competitor? Let’s take a closer look… Starting with the engine! 

While the Venom GT & F5 were both powered by the same twin-turbo V8, Hennessey instead opted to fit the Blackbird with an all-new, 6.2-litre naturally-aspirated V8. This produces between 800 and 850hp, with all of this power sent to the rear wheels only via a 6-speed manual! 

What’s more, it revs to 9000RPM (the highest-revving naturally-aspirated V8 on any road car), can hit 60mph in 2.5 seconds (about the same as the CC850), and it has a top speed of 220mph!

When it comes to the design, the Blackbird is largely just made from carbon fibre, which means it only weighs in at 1,360kg. The sculpted doors mirror the shape of the SR-71, as does the sky glass roof, along with the rear stabilisers, which automatically deploy once you hit 71 mph. Speaking of the rear end, the Blackbird also comes with diamond-shaped, quad tailpipes, and the diamond shape is mirrored in the headlights as well. All-in, this long and low hypercar looks absolutely incredible! 

Step inside, and it feels like you’ve stepped back in time - there are no screens anywhere! The Blackbird comes with analogue dials and a built-in mount for your phone. It also has an old-fashioned key, as well as twin carbon fibre seats, and 4(!) cupholders. The swooping-style design reminds us of the Bugatti Tourbillon, and the overhead switches once again hark back to the SR-71. 

But of course, it doesn’t come cheap - the Blackbird costs from $2,500,000, and it’ll be limited to just 71 units. The question is, would you choose it over a Koenigsegg CC850? Let us know in the comments! Hennessey has released an all-new Koenigsegg competitor - the Blackbird!

videos.title: Is Longevity a Lie?
videos.summary_source_text:
Is Longevity a Lie? Is longevity a big lie?

The idea is simple: eat well, exercise, manage your stress, have good relationships... and you'll live to 100.

The problem is, that's not what the data show.

The New England Centenarian Study, one of the best studies we have on people who actually make it to 100, found that exceptional longevity is largely genetic. You really do need to win the genetic lottery.

What's even weirder is that plenty of centenarians smoked, drank, never exercised, and lived pretty normal lives. They don't avoid heart disease, cancer, or dementia. They just tend to get them later than everyone else. Their genes seem to buy them another decade.

That's why I think the longevity movement is a little misleading.

What we're really talking about is healthspan.

Exercise, good nutrition, sleep, and stress management probably won't turn you into a centenarian. But they can absolutely help you stay stronger, healthier, and more independent for the years you do have. Is longevity a big lie?

I would never have guessed there were eggs in it! It's incredibly delicious! A must-try if you like protein desserts.

4 hard-boiled eggs.
1 tbsp stevia. ½ cup (125 ml) milk.
⅓ cup (40 g) unsweetened cocoa powder.
You’ll only need a few simple ingredients to make this delicious dessert.
The best part is—there’s no baking required.
